“Virtue is a state concerned with choice, lying in a mean relative…” — Aristotle (Q0012)

An English quotation associated with Nicomachean Ethics II.6, organized here under meaning.

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with Nicomachean Ethics II.6, within the Peripatetic School tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of meaning, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Aristotle's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
